docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Traditional task management systems often struggle with scalability and data isolation when serving multiple client organizations. Single-tenant deployments are costly to maintain, while poorly designed multi-tenant architectures risk data leakage. Furthermore, basic task trackers lack the auditability and role-based governance required by enterprise teams, leading to unmanaged access and untrackable changes.

docs.title: Proposed Solution
docs.text:
TaskVault addresses these challenges with a multi-tenant, API-first backend.

  • It enforces strict data isolation using Organization IDs across all entities.
  • It implements a 3-tier role system (Super Admin, Tenant Admin, User) to ensure granular access control.
  • It provides immutable audit logs for task history and soft-deletion mechanisms to guarantee data integrity and recovery.
  • It integrates Razorpay for seamless subscription billing and Celery/Redis for high-performance background processing.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text: TaskVault is a multi-tenant application where data is strictly isolated by Organization.

docs.title: Core Tenets
docs.text:
• A User belongs to exactly one Organization.
  • A Task belongs to exactly one Organization.
  • Cross-tenant access is strictly blocked. Users cannot view or modify data from other organizations.

docs.title: User Roles
docs.text:
1. SUPER_ADMIN: Platform owner. Manages Organizations and Tenant Admins. Cannot participate in daily task management.
  2. TENANT_ADMIN: Organization manager. Manages Users and Tasks within their Organization.
  3. USER: Standard employee. Manages their own tasks and assignments.

docs.title: Key capabilities include
docs.text:
• Multi-Tenancy: Complete data isolation per organization.
  • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Granular permissions for Super Admins, Tenant Admins, and standard Users.
  • Subscription Management: Integration with Razorpay for handling premium organization subscriptions.
  • Audit Trails: Immutable history logging for critical task changes.
  • Scalable Architecture: Optimized for performance with database indexing and efficient query structures.

docs.title: 1. Multi-Tenancy Architecture
docs.text:
• Organization-First Approach: Every user and task is scoped to a specific organization.
  • Data Isolation: Strict permission checks ensure users can never access data outside their organization.
  • Tenant Management: Super Admins can oversee all organizations, while Tenant Admins manage their specific instance.

docs.title: 2. Advanced Permission System
docs.text:
• Super Admin: System-wide access, mostly for maintenance and oversight.
  • Tenant Admin: Complete control over their organization's users, tasks, and billing.
  • User: varying levels of access to tasks (create, view, edit) based on ownership and assignment.

docs.title: 3. Subscription & Billing
docs.text:
• Lifetime Premium Plans: Organizations can upgrade to premium status.
  • Payment Processing: Secure integration with Razorpay for payment capture and verification.
  • Webhook Handling: Robust processing of payment events (success/failure) to maintain state consistency.

docs.title: 4. Task Management
docs.text:
• Subtasks: Support for breaking down tasks into smaller subtasks (1-level nesting).
  • History Tracking: every status or priority change is recorded in TasksHistory for accountability.
  • Soft Deletion: All major entities (Users, Tasks, Comments) support soft deletion to prevent accidental data loss.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Goal Description Multi-Tenancy Secure isolation of data across different organizations. RBAC distinct roles (Super Admin, Tenant Admin, User) with specific privilege sets. Auditability Full tracking of task mutations and payment events. Monetization Built-in subscription flows for premium organization features. Security JWT authentication, email verification, and secure password handling. Performance Optimized database schema with appropriate indexing for common queries.

(Role Required: Tenant Admin / Super Admin)

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text:
TaskVault follows a layered backend architecture that separates responsibilities clearly and keeps business logic maintainable.

Request Flow:

Client → URL Router → DRF Views (Permissions & Auth) → Serializers (Validation) → Service Layer (Business Logic) → Models (Data Structure) → PostgreSQL Database

docs.title: Architectural Principles
docs.text:
• API-First Design: All functionalities are exposed via RESTful endpoints.
  • Separation of Concerns: Logic is decoupled into Views, Services, and Models.
  • Multi-Tenancy: Data is logically isolated by organization_id.
  • Soft Deletion: Entities are marked as deleted rather than physically removed.
  • Immutable Audit Logs: Critical changes (task status, payments) are permanently recorded.

docs.title: 1. Core Framework
docs.text:
• Django 6.0: The backbone of the application, utilizing its ORM for database abstraction and signal system.
  • Django REST Framework (DRF): Powers the API layer with robust Serializers for validation and ViewSets for logic.
  • PostgreSQL (psycopg 3 driver): Primary relational database chosen for its reliability and JSONB support (used in Webhook payloads).

docs.title: 2. Asynchronous & Background Processing
docs.text:
• Celery: Distributed task queue handling long-running operations.
    • Tasks: sending emails (users.tasks), processing webhooks (subscriptions.tasks).
  • Celery Beat: Scheduler for periodic maintenance jobs.
    • Jobs: reconcile_pending_subscriptions (Hourly), hard_delete_unverified_users (Daily), clear_blacklisted_tokens (Daily).
  • Redis: In-memory data store acting as:
    • Message Broker: For Celery task queues.
    • Cache Backend: Using django-redis for caching API responses and sessions.

docs.title: 3. Email Service
docs.text:
• Brevo (formerly Sendinblue): Transactional email provider via SMTP relay.
    • Used for Invitation links, Password Resets, and Email Verification.

docs.title: 4. Middleware
docs.text: • LoggingMiddleware (core.middleware): Custom middleware that intercepts every request/response loop to log metadata (User ID, Path, Status Code, Duration) to JSON logs for observability.

docs.title: 4. Payments
docs.text:
• Razorpay Integration: Handles all payment processing.
    • Uses Webhooks for real-time status updates (e.g., payment.captured, payment.failed).
    • Dedicated webhook_events table ensures idempotency.

docs.title: Modules Breakdown
docs.text: Module Description Key Components core Foundation layer. LoggingMiddleware, JSONFormatter, Custom Exceptions, IsSuperAdmin/IsTenantAdmin Permissions. users Identity & Access Management. User, Organization models. auth endpoints (/login, /verify-otp), RegisterAPIView. tasks Project Management domain. Task, Comment, TaskHistory models. TaskViewSet with complex filtering logic. subscriptions Billing & Revenue. Subscription, Payment, WebhookEvent. razorpay utilities, atomic transaction services.

docs.title: Authentication & Security
docs.text: TaskVault uses JWT (JSON Web Token) for stateless, secure authentication. All protected endpoints require a valid access token in the header.

docs.title: Authentication Mechanism
docs.text:
• Access Token: Short-lived (e.g., 2 hours). Used for API access.
  • Refresh Token: Long-lived (e.g., 7 days). Used to obtain new access tokens.
  • Header Format: Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>

docs.title: 1. Registration & Verification
docs.text:
1. Register: User POSTs to /api/v1/auth/tenant/<tenant_id>/register/ (or via invite link).
  2. Email Verification: System sends a verification link to the user's email.
  3. Verify: User clicks link -> POST /api/v1/auth/email-verification/verify/ with token.
  4. Constraint: Users cannot login until is_email_verified=True.

docs.title: 2. Login with OTP (2FA)
docs.text:
1. Login Request: POST /api/v1/auth/login/ with email/password.
  2. OTP Challenge: If valid, system sends an OTP to email and returns a temporary session hash (not yet a token).
  3. Verify OTP: POST /api/v1/auth/login/verify-otp/ with email, OTP, and session hash.
  4. Resend OTP: If expired, POST /api/v1/auth/login/resend-otp/.
  5. Success: Server returns access and refresh tokens.

docs.title: 3. Password Management
docs.text:
• Forgot Password: POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password/ triggers an email with a reset link.
  • Reset Password: POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password/<token>/ allows setting a new password.
  • Change Password: Authenticated users use POST /api/v1/users/change-password/.

docs.title: 4. Invitations
docs.text:
• Tenant Admins generate invites via POST /api/v1/users/invite/.
  • New users register via POST /api/v1/auth/invite/<token>/register/.

docs.title: Refreshing Tokens
docs.text: When the access token expires, use the refresh token to get a new pair: POST /api/v1/auth/refresh/

docs.title: Logout (Blacklisting)
docs.text: To securely logout, the client must send the refresh token to be blacklisted: POST /api/v1/auth/logout/ Effect: The refresh token is invalidated immediately.

docs.title: Security Features
docs.text:
• OTP Rate Limiting: Prevents brute-force on 2FA.
  • Token Blacklist: Invalidates tokens on logout.
  • Password Hashing: PBKDF2 with SHA256.
  • Strict Role Check: Middleware/Permissions verify Role + Organization Status on every request.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
TaskVault has evolved into a comprehensive, multi-tenant SaaS backend. It successfully addresses the complex requirements of data isolation, role-based security, and subscription tracking. By leveraging a clean layered architecture and explicit permission classes, the system ensures both scalability and maintainability.

The move to an Organization-based model allows TaskVault to serve not just individuals but entire teams and companies securely.

docs.title: Future Scope
docs.text:
While the core system is robust, future enhancements could include:

  • Team Management: Groups within an Organization for finer-grained sharing.
  • Recurring Subscriptions: Moving beyond "Lifetime" plans to monthly/yearly billing.
  • Notifications: Email/Push alerts for task deadlines and assignments.
  • Advanced Analytics: Dashboards for Tenant Admins to view productivity metrics.

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text: TaskVault uses a relational database (PostgreSQL recommended) with a multi-tenant schema design. All primary entities are linked to an Organization.

docs.title: 1. Organizations & Users
docs.text: Table Description ORGANIZATIONS The top-level tenant entity. Contains subscription status (is_premium). USERS Members of an organization. Roles: SUPER_ADMIN, TENANT_ADMIN, USER.

docs.title: 2. Task Management
docs.text: Table Description TASKS Core work unit. Linked to an Org, Owner, and Assignee. Supports subtasks. TASKS_HISTORY Audit log for status/priority changes. COMMENTS Discussion threads on tasks.

docs.title: 3. Billing (Subscriptions)
docs.text: Table Description SUBSCRIPTIONS Tracks the premium status of an organization. One-to-One with Org. PAYMENTS Log of all payment attempts (success or failure) via Razorpay. WEBHOOK_EVENTS Raw storage of incoming webhook data for auditing and debugging.

docs.title: Permissions & Access Control
docs.text: TaskVault employs a robust Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system with three distinct roles. Permissions are enforced at the object level and verified via custom permission classes in core/permissions.py.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text: This section outlines the functional and non-functional requirements of the TaskVault system.

docs.title: 1. Multi-Tenancy & Organizations
docs.text:
• The system must isolate data (Tasks, Users, Comments) per Organization.
  • New registrations must automatically provision an Organization.
  • An Organization can have a Subscription Plan (Lifetime Premium).
  • If an Organization’s subscription fails or is inactive, access triggers appropriate blocks.

docs.title: 2. User Management
docs.text:
• Roles: Must support Super Admin, Tenant Admin, and User.
  • Authentication: JWT-based login, refresh, and logout (blacklist).
  • Email Verification: Users should verify email before becoming fully active.
  • Tenant Admin Control: Tenant Admins can manage users within their organization only.

docs.title: 3. Task Management
docs.text:
• Hierarchical Tasks: Support for parent tasks and subtasks (1-level nesting).
  • Ownership: Tasks must have an owner and an assignee.
  • Visibility:
    • Tenant Admin: View all tasks in the Org.
    • User: View only Owned or Assigned tasks.
  • Soft Deletion: Tasks are marked deleted, not removed from DB.

docs.title: 4. Billing & Payments
docs.text:
• Integration with Razorpay for payment processing.
  • Webhook support to handle payment success/failure asynchronously.
  • Ability to upgrade an Organization to "Premium" status.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Strict object-level permissions (core/permissions.py).
  • No cross-tenant data leakage.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
• Immutable History: Logic for TasksHistory must prevent modification.
  • Soft Deletion: Ensuring referential integrity even after user/task deletion.

docs.title: Task History System
docs.text: TaskVault maintains an immutable audit log for task updates.

docs.title: What Is Recorded
docs.text:
• Old and new task status
  • Old and new task priority
  • User who made the change
  • Timestamp of change

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
• History records are never updated or deleted
  • History is created only when meaningful changes occur
  • History is read-only via API

docs.title: Access Rules
docs.text:
• Admin can view history of any task
  • User can view history only for tasks assigned to them

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text:
1. Super Admin -> onboards Tenant Admin (Organization created automatically).
  2. Tenant Admin -> creates Normal User (linked to the same Organization).

docs.title: Account Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Invitation: Users can be invited via email tokens.
  • Verification: New users must verify their email (is_email_verified=True) to access full features.
  • Restoration: Soft-deleted users can be Restored by Tenant Admins using the /users/{id}/restore/ endpoint, recovering their access and associations.
  • Hard Deletion: A scheduled Celery task permanently removes users who have been soft-deleted for > 30 days (configurable).

docs.title: A. Creation & Assignment
docs.text:
• Tenant Admin: Can create tasks and assign them to any active user in the Org.
  • Normal User: Can create tasks but MUST be the assignee (Self-Assignment only).

docs.title: B. Subtasks
docs.text:
• Nesting Limit: Max depth is 1. (Parent -> Subtask).
  • Ownership Rule: Users can only create subtasks for parents they OWN.
  • Admin Rule: Tenant Admins can create subtasks for any task in their Org.

docs.title: C. Updates
docs.text:
• Status Change: Updating status to COMPLETED is BLOCKED if the task has active (incomplete) Subtasks. All subtasks must be completed first.
  • Deleted Tasks: Updating a soft-deleted task is BLOCKED for everyone (returns 404/403).

docs.title: D. Deletion
docs.text:
• Parent/Subtask Constraint: You CANNOT delete a Parent Task if it has active Subtasks. You must delete the subtasks first.
  • Effects: Searching for the task returns 404 for Normal Users. Admins can look it up by ID (Read-Only).

docs.title: 3. Organization Deactivation Workflow
docs.text:
If an Organization is marked is_active=False (e.g., for non-payment or policy violation):

  1. Login Block:
    • Tenant Admins attempting login receive: "Your organization is deactivated please contact super admin to reactive the organization".
    • Normal Users attempting login receive: "Your organization is deactivated".
  2. Admin Freeze:
    • Super Admins cannot create new Tenant Admins for this Org.
    • Super Admins cannot delete existing Tenant Admins for this Org.
  3. Reactivation:
    • Super Admin patches is_active=True. Access is instantly restored.

docs.title: 4. Comment Management Utils
docs.text:
• Create: Users can comment on any task they can view (Own/Assigned).
  • View: Visibility matches Task visibility.
  • Update/Delete: Users can only edit/delete their own comments. Tenant Admins can delete any comment (moderation).

docs.title: 5. Edge Cases & Constraints
docs.text:
1. Unique Titles: Task titles must be unique per User constraints (normalized case-insensitive check).
  2. Past Deadlines: Creating/Updating a task with a deadline in the past is blocked.
  3. Self-Assignment: Normal Users trying to assign tasks to colleagues will face a Validation Error.
  4. Deleted Entity Interaction:
    • You cannot assign a task to a deleted user.
    • You cannot create a subtask under a deleted parent.
